g.text: truST Runtime: Admitted Ownership and Hosted Cycle
Hosted cycle: borrowed adapters, common scheduler
Device resource loop: one thread, no operating system (spec 34 STATE-08)
Program loading: transfer, checks, commit, reply, restart (spec 34 5.1, 11.2, PORT-05)
framing, CRC, types and bounded analysis
immutable VM, registry and optional register plans
private io / ads / opcua / retain / metrics / watchdog
checked types, paths, lifetimes and work
construction, budgets, fault and IR selection
HIR types/source retained only in full host
clock, deadline, observer, captured register config
Installed storage and executable schema have no raw mutable getter.
Full/development keep hosted tools and services; runtime-only owns the
same core state with a thin std clock/deadline adapter and no compiler/HIR graph.
Every composition retains the full PLC function set.
Export copies admitted artifact data; it never serializes current PLC values.
shared bytecode opcode loop; no-register calls stay in-loop
leased parent scratch and common completion
libm numerics and full standard library
Both representations use one entry allowance and the same deadline,
frame cleanup, reference policy and bytecode instruction costs.
Yield and resume do not re-charge bytecode or repeat block-entry hooks.
The stack dispatcher and register-enabled pump keep native stack use
independent of admitted POU depth. In no-register builds, native stack
callees push frames and restore cursor continuations inside the same loop.
Both return through one call binding/completion owner and opcode interpreter.
No lowering, source evaluation or first-use compilation runs in RUN.
Optimization fallback never removes PLC functionality.
logical clock, supervision, STOP and simulation
physical inputs; debug I/O writes and forces
then ADS / OPC UA cached inputs
then variable/I/O forces, protocol capture, debug snapshot
flat Q commits after every driver succeeds
health, CycleEnd, metrics and cycle count
Failure before successful submission restores touched flat Q windows only.
Marker/hierarchical effects keep the established hosted rollback domain.
A late deadline/telemetry fault cannot undo outputs accepted by drivers.
Invalid management requests produce WriteRejected, not a PLC fault;
actual execution/adapter/deadline failures follow the fault policy.
serves the control link between scans and while Stopped;
takes pause / resume / bytecode.reload / restart / shutdown at the program's next boundary
(next scan, paused interval, 10 ms faulted poll) as the host's scan thread does;
scans when due, idle work, feeds the hardware watchdog,
then waits for the next boundary, the feed interval or a wake;
Running / Paused / Stopped / Faulted by the shared supervisor,
cycle and task events, task / program / overrun metrics
events.tail and faults written event by event
retain save, restart cold / warm, task timing,
installation generation (the loop gives it to the Live Values
after each restart and when it takes a program),
inputs before the scan, outputs at the engine's publication,
safe outputs written into the output image, then driven;
DeviceServices: scan deadline on the monotonic clock,
no wall clock until T6 (CURRENT_DT refused at admission);
device_limits from the region and heap sizes
access, audit, wall clock, status values,
chip firmware, or the host's transcript parity test
line framing, frames of 8,192 bytes on a chip's USB,
an oversized request dropped and answered once,
one reply in flight, the 1 s stall rule
shutdown stops the program (safe outputs, then the retain save) at its
next boundary and the device keeps serving the link; restart then starts
the installed program as a new trust-runtime process would, with empty
records and logical time from zero. Without an installed program
(Runner::stopped) the loop serves the link Stopped and refuses restart
with the reason. trust-runtime on a computer keeps its
threads and calls the same shared rules; its scheduler keeps its own
scheduler::Clock (StdClock), and only its metrics uptime clock and its
ControlState wall clock implement the core port traits.
next generation of the lineage, logical time and process images carried,
a congruent candidate keeps retained FB instances and references live,
any other migrates a snapshot by name or is refused,
the saved snapshot of the retain store applied over it
checked owner images + every driver attempt
STRN v3: logical values + physical layout/backing
selected transports / T0 SHM / Linux RT posture
no tasks or outputs; serves reads and config;
shutdown stops it as a running program (safe outputs, retain save)
and leaves it Stopped with the fault reported until the next start
shutdown stops the program (safe outputs, then the retain save);
the process stays up with its control server, web UI and services;
no tasks or outputs, polls every 10 ms for restart or exit;
restart loads the installed bundle again, as a new process loads it;
the process ends only on SIGINT / SIGTERM, shutdown with exit true or hang action abort
independent thread reads the published deadline;
Resource-only edits do not execute initializers or reconstruct PLC values.
Binding-only edits preserve task timing; explicit task replacement samples
SINGLE and resets registration timing while retaining thread identity history.
Failure or discarded candidate leaves the installed state unchanged.
the bytes the store commits into an empty store
one upload staged in RAM in parts of 4,096 bytes,
every part CRC-32 checked, the whole upload SHA-256 checked;
ids: boot number + sequence; a reset ends every transfer
Admin; first failing check is the reply:
params, hung scan, resource not Stopped (resource_not_running),
no program store (unsupported request), complete upload taken
1 container: magic, header CRC, length, entries, payload CRCs
3 retained values against the newest checkpoint or retain file (G13)
4 dry-run preparation with the admitted limits
nothing is written until all four pass
slot = the one without the newest committed container, or A;
erase units, program payloads, header and first half of the magic,
read back, program the second half of the magic = commit point
Chip: the commit is the reply in flight (runner/install.rs)
one step in each pass of the loop (one erase unit, or at most 256 bytes
programmed or read back), watchdog fed;
no request is read until the installed reply is written;
a failed step is the reply
a deployment of the program alone: admit first, stage bundles/label, temporary file + rename per file,
rename of current = commit point, then previous, then prune;
web deploy, web rollback and program.install, Stopped only (Q11)
two slots A and B: read, program, erase
one FlashOwner shares the flash with the checkpoint slots
reads both headers: the committed TRSTA002 with the highest sequence wins;
TRSTA001 is not committed and its slot is named in the reason;
a damaged newest container refuses the boot, no fallback (Q12):
params (bytes or transfer), hung scan, Stopped refused, upload taken;
replies reloaded / reload timeout / resource stopped /
commit outcome unknown; shared by every runtime
queues the change for the scan thread; waits 5 s for it to be taken
and 60 s for the commit; memory only.
Chip: the online change is the reply in flight (runner/online_change.rs)
queued by the loop when the request is admitted; the loop reads no request until it ends;
at the next boundary, after the stop and the queued pauses and resumes, before a pending restart:
take (withdrawn with reload timeout after 5 s), prepare, commit, drop the old program last;
memory only: a stop and a restart load the installed container (spec 34 11.3, STATE-08)
module prepared with device_limits of the heap's room less the reserve (8 KiB, and the newest
checkpoint's payload when the record keeps retained values),
the upload freed at once (insufficient memory otherwise); bindings checked against
the lines of the running record; built from the running state over an empty process I/O
and the newest checkpoint as the saved snapshot (ProgramMemory::replace);
safe state checked; no pin claimed, no output written;
a refusal leaves the running program as it was
process I/O and checkpoint store change places with the candidate's empty ones
(no line released or claimed, no output written); logical time kept, scan counter 0,
queued writes and forces cleared; the old program is dropped last
The reply of program.install carries status installed, sequence, program_sha256 and bytes.
On a chip it comes after the whole commit, up to 0.4 s per 4 KiB erase unit,
so a client reads it with the bound of spec 11 6.8.1 and not with 750 ms.
An interrupted install keeps the previous program selected (DEPLOY-03).
conditions, watches, queued writes and forces
Snapshot mutation never copies back into live invocation locals.
Candidate construction emits no active debugger observations.
Debug pause does not grant mutable schema or raw PLC storage access.
• web auth required for session bootstrap
• writes allowed only in debug mode
• accept loop + HTTP lifecycle in web/server.rs
• incomplete bodies cannot occupy the read lane
• route handlers split by concern in web/*_routes.rs
async config hydration + ARIA route state
The scan thread performs no ADS
wire operations off the scan thread
admitted resource transaction before worker start
const folding / source lowering / detached debug evaluation

one frame at a time, between scans

cycle deadline; declares a hung scan Faulted
the installed reply is written when the last step is done

at a boundary, the running program stays installed

queued next-scan application; stale destinations reject
Source ownership view; validation, rendering and hardware evidence are separate.
Production execution uses the canonical shared core and an admitted artifact.
Host services borrow checked ports; no second mutable PLC store or dispatcher.
Retained state remains ordinary global/instance storage with declared policy.
Platform capabilities and performance must be verified in their selected composition.
